newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY TO FIRMER WITH SWAPS UP.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY TO FIRMER WITH SWAPS UP.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel oil barges were steady to a touch stronger early on Wednesday on good bunker demand and with swaps up to $1 stronger, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $95.50 for RMG material and $96 and $96.25 fob ARA for refinery material compared with Tuesday's trade level of $94.50 to $96 a tonne.
"There's a lot of bunker enquiries, it was just physical coverage," a trader said, adding the highest numbers were done by two majors in Rotterdam.
Low sulphur fuel barges continued to slumber with a lack of demand but levels were notionally unchanged.
"Sellers are still at $97.50 and looking for bids," one trader said, adding that the offers were kept just a little above the high sulphur barge quotes.

Russian high sulphur cracked cargoes, said to be in low supply, were offered steady at two means +$1, but sellers said that meant a better price with the two means quote higher on the back of the rising barge prices.

"Barges are stronger so cif prices will be stronger too," a trader showing an M-100 cracked cargo said, adding he bought a cargo of high sulphur high density fuel from a refiner at $86 cif on Tuesday.
Plentiful supply of Russian high sulphur straight-run coupled with little buying interest drove premiums a little lower.
Traders said M-100 was offered at two means +$3 compared with a premium of $4 over the quote a day earlier while E-4 was steady to a little weaker at three means flat to $2 over the quote.
